t: Under Section 2(7)(i), a person who uses goods with the approval of the buyer, without having paid for them, is:
o: A consumer only if the goods are under warranty
Excluded from the definition of consumer
Included as a consumer, being a user of the goods with the buyer's approval
A consumer only if a minor
e: The definition includes any user of goods other than the buyer when such use is made with the approval of the buyer, so family members using a purchased appliance are consumers.

t: A weaver buys a power loom under a bank loan payable in 36 instalments and operates it himself for his living. Which two features of Section 2(7) bring him within 'consumer'?
o: He is an individual and the loom is new
Deferred payment is covered, and self-employment livelihood is excluded from 'commercial purpose'
Goods are movable and purchased from a dealer
e: Consideration under any system of deferred payment is expressly covered, and the Explanation excludes from 'commercial purpose' goods used exclusively to earn a livelihood by self-employment.

t: Under the 1986 Act a complaint was ordinarily filed at the place of purchase or the seller's registered office. The 2019 Act changed this by permitting filing:
o: Only at the place of the opposite party's branch
At the place where the consumer resides or works
e: The 2019 Act gives the consumer the flexibility to file at the jurisdictional Commission of his place of residence or work.

t: The Central Consumer Protection Authority is described in the 2019 Act as:
o: A quasi-judicial forum to adjudicate consumer complaints
A regulatory authority with wide powers of enforcement, including an investigation wing
An advisory body under the Ministry
e: The CCPA is a regulator with powers of investigation, suo-motu action, recall, reimbursement, licence cancellation and class action, distinct from the adjudicating Commissions.

t: The term 'product seller' under the 2019 Act includes:
o: Only a retailer with a physical shop
A person involved in placing the product for a commercial purpose, including e-commerce platforms
e: 'Product seller' is defined widely to include any person involved in placing the product for a commercial purpose, and hence covers e-commerce platforms.

t: Which of the following was newly brought within 'unfair trade practice' by the 2019 Act?
o: Disclosure of a consumer's personal information given in confidence, unless permitted by law
e: The 2019 Act's broad definition of unfair trade practice specifically includes sharing personal information given by the consumer in confidence, unless such disclosure is made under any other law.

t: A company and its brand ambassador are each proceeded against for a first misleading advertisement. The maximum monetary penalty the CCPA can impose on each is:
e: The CCPA may impose a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh on a manufacturer or an endorser for a first false or misleading advertisement, with imprisonment up to two years.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Section 147(1)(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 requires that a policy complying with Chapter XI must be issued by:
o: An insurer approved by the State Transport Authority
Any insurer registered with the Registrar of Companies
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 147(1)(a) mandates that the policy be issued by a person who is an 'authorised insurer', a term defined in Section 145.

t: A complaint alleging an unfair contract where the consideration paid is ₹12 crore lies before the:
e: Complaints against unfair contracts where consideration exceeds ₹10 crore are within the NCDRC's original jurisdiction under Section 58(1)(a)(ii).

t: The pecuniary jurisdiction of Consumer Commissions under the 2019 Act is determined by:
o: The value of goods or services paid as consideration
The sum insured under the policy
The net worth of the opposite party
The compensation claimed in the complaint
e: Unlike the 1986 Act (value of goods plus compensation claimed), the 2019 Act uses the value of goods or services paid as consideration, which for insurance means the premium.

t: A revision petition before the NCDRC under Section 58(1)(b) is filed within 90 days, as provided by:
o: Regulation 14(1)(i) of the Consumer Protection (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations, 2020
e: The Act does not itself fix the period for revision; Regulation 14(1)(i) of the 2020 Regulations prescribes 90 days for revision petitions.

t: A State Commission disposes of a consumer complaint on 10 May. The insurer, wishing to appeal to the NCDRC, must file within the normal period by:
e: Appeals from the State Commission to the NCDRC under Section 51(1) must be filed within 30 days, i.e. by 9 June; delay beyond that requires condonation.

t: Which section of the 2019 Act deals with the consequences of non-compliance with an order of a Consumer Commission?
e: Section 72 penalises non-compliance with Commission orders; appeals against such orders lie under Section 73 within 30 days.

t: A consumer complaint is filed 2 years and 3 months after the cause of action. The Commission:
o: Must transfer it to the civil court
May entertain it only if the consideration exceeds ₹50 lakh
Must dismiss it, as limitation cannot be condoned
May entertain it if sufficient cause for the delay is shown under Section 69
e: Section 69 fixes two years but empowers the Commission to condone delay where the complainant satisfies it that there was sufficient cause for not filing within time.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: Which of the following persons' liability is insured under a Section 147 policy?
o: The person or classes of persons specified in the policy, to the extent specified in sub-section (2)
e: Section 147(1)(b) requires the policy to insure the person or classes of persons specified in the policy (e.g. owner and any person driving with permission) to the extent in sub-section (2).

t: Compare the old and amended clause (1)(b)(ii) of Section 147. The amendment:
o: Widened cover from passengers of a public service vehicle to passengers of any transport vehicle, excluding gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle
e: The amended clause extends compulsory passenger cover to all transport vehicles (including goods carriages carrying fare-paying/entitled passengers) but excludes gratuitous passengers of goods vehicles.

t: Under Section 64VA, the control level of solvency (required solvency ratio) that an insurer must maintain is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VA requires assets to exceed liabilities by the required solvency margin; IRDAI prescribes a control level solvency ratio of 150% (1.5 times), below which regulatory action follows.

t: A bus on a public road hits a cyclist who is thrown into an adjoining private field and dies there. The insurer argues the death occurred on private land. Under Section 147 the argument:
o: Fails only if the cyclist was a passenger
Succeeds, as the death was not in a public place
Fails, because the act or omission leading to the accident occurred in a public place
Succeeds unless the field was open to the public
e: The Explanation deems the death to arise out of use of the vehicle in a public place when the causative act occurred in a public place, irrespective of where the victim was at the time.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Limits of liability
t: A fleet owner opts to restrict TPPD cover to the statutory limit under the old Section 147(2)(b) in exchange for a premium discount. His truck damages a parked car (₹1.2 lakh) and a roadside kiosk (₹3,000) in one accident. The insurer's liability for property damage is:
e: The statutory limit of ₹6,000 applies per accident for damage to third-party property; the insurer's liability in this accident is capped at ₹6,000 and the balance falls on the insured.

t: The amended Section 147(2) uses the expression 'grievous hurt'. Under Section 145 of the MV Act this term has the meaning assigned in:
o: Section 320 of the Indian Penal Code / corresponding BNS provision
e: Section 145 adopts the meaning of 'grievous hurt' from Section 320 of the IPC (now the corresponding provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita).

topic: MV Act s.147 – Certificate of insurance
t: An insurer issues a policy document but omits to issue the certificate of insurance. For the purposes of Chapter XI the policy is:
o: Fully effective, as the policy wording is complete
Of no effect unless and until the certificate is issued
e: Section 147(3) makes the certificate of insurance a condition for the policy to have effect under the Chapter; the certificate is what the driver produces to prove cover.

t: The amended cover-note sub-section of Section 147 refers to cover notes issued under the Chapter or under:
o: The rules or regulations made thereunder
e: The amended text (sub-section (5)) refers to cover notes issued 'under the provisions of this Chapter or the rules or regulations made thereunder', adding 'regulations' to the earlier wording.

topic: MV Act s.147 – Requirements of policy
t: A policy issued by a company that is not registered with IRDAI as an insurer is produced before the Claims Tribunal. Under Section 147(1)(a) such a policy:
o: Is valid if countersigned by the RTO
Satisfies the Chapter if the premium was paid
Does not comply with Chapter XI, as it is not issued by an authorised insurer
Is valid for third-party death only
e: Only a policy issued by an authorised insurer (one registered under the Insurance Act) satisfies Section 147(1)(a); the vehicle is otherwise uninsured for Chapter XI purposes.

t: Under Section 164 of the amended MV Act, the claimant seeking ₹5 lakh for death is:
o: Required to obtain a criminal conviction first
Required to prove the deceased's income
Required to prove negligence of the driver
Not required to plead or establish any wrongful act, neglect or default of the owner
e: Section 164(2) provides that the claimant need not plead or establish any wrongful act, neglect or default; the compensation is on a no-fault basis.

t: The 2019 amendment inserted Section 164B providing for a:
o: Motor Vehicle Accident Fund for compulsory insurance cover to all road users
Solatium Fund administered by GIC Re
e: Section 164B creates the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund to provide compulsory insurance cover to all road users, including golden-hour treatment and hit-and-run compensation.

t: The period of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963 for a civil suit against an insurer on a policy of insurance is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Article 44 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act provides three years for suits against an insurer on a policy, running from the occurrence of the loss or the date the claim is denied.

t: Under Section 166(4) as amended in 2019, the Claims Tribunal shall treat as an application for compensation:
o: The accident report submitted by the police officer under Section 159
e: Section 166(4) requires the Tribunal to treat the police accident report (Detailed Accident Report) as an application for compensation, speeding up adjudication.

t: In Pranay Sethi (2017) the Supreme Court fixed conventional heads for death claims: loss of estate ₹15,000, funeral ₹15,000 and loss of consortium ₹40,000, to be enhanced by:
e: The Constitution Bench directed that the conventional amounts be enhanced at 10% every three years to account for inflation.

t: A vehicle is sold on 1 March and the new owner applies for transfer of the certificate of insurance on 20 March. Under Section 157 of the MV Act:
o: The insurer may cancel the policy for late application
The policy is void from 1 March
The certificate and policy are deemed transferred to the transferee from the date of transfer; the transferee should apply within 14 days for change of particulars
e: Section 157 deems the certificate and policy transferred with the vehicle (for third-party purposes) from the date of transfer; the transferee must apply within 14 days to have the particulars changed.

t: Section 64VB(5) read with Rules 58 and 59 of the Insurance Rules, 1939 permits risk to be assumed before receipt of premium in cases such as:
o: Government bodies and certain insurances where a bank guarantee or deposit is furnished
e: The exceptions under the Rules include risks of Central/State Government and certain public bodies, and cases where premium is guaranteed by bank guarantee or cash deposit.

t: Section 64UM also prescribes that a claim must be settled within a specified period of receipt of the survey report, failing which the insurer:
o: Must refer the matter to the Ombudsman
Is liable to pay interest on the claim amount for the delay
e: The 2015 amendment to Section 64UM requires settlement within the period specified by regulations and liability for interest in case of delay, reinforced by the PPHI regulations' 2% above bank rate.

t: The General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972 brought general insurance under government ownership with effect from:
e: GIBNA 1972 nationalised general insurance from 1 January 1973, creating GIC and its four subsidiaries (National, New India, Oriental and United India).

t: A penalty of up to ₹1 crore for contravention of provisions of the Insurance Act (where no specific penalty is provided) is laid down in:
e: Section 102 empowers IRDAI to impose a penalty up to ₹1 lakh per day of default, subject to a maximum of ₹1 crore, for failure to comply with the Act, rules, regulations or directions.

t: A policyholder nominates his wife under a life policy. The relevant provision of the Insurance Act, 1938 is:
e: Section 39 governs nomination by the policyholder; after the 2015 amendment nominees who are parents, spouse or children are 'beneficial nominees' entitled to the proceeds.

t: Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 confers on the Authority the duty to:
o: Underwrite risks of the PSU insurers
Fix tariffs for all classes of insurance
Regulate, promote and ensure orderly growth of the insurance business and reinsurance business
e: Section 14 lists IRDAI's duties, powers and functions, including issuing registration, protecting policyholders, regulating intermediaries and ensuring orderly growth.

t: A policyholder returns a two-year health policy within the free-look period. Under the 2024 regulations the insurer refunds the premium after deducting:
o: Proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, stamp duty and medical examination expenses
e: On free-look cancellation the insurer refunds the premium less the proportionate risk premium for the period on cover, stamp duty charges and expenses of medical examination, if any.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 framework, a policyholder's grievance received by an insurer must be resolved within:
e: The 2024 regulations require insurers to resolve grievances within 14 days of receipt; unresolved grievances may be escalated to the Bima Bharosa portal and the Ombudsman.

t: The body that administers the Insurance Ombudsman scheme after the 2021 amendment is the:
e: The 2021 amendment renamed the Executive Council of Insurers as the Council for Insurance Ombudsmen, which administers the 17 Ombudsman offices.

t: Which of the following complaints is outside the Insurance Ombudsman's jurisdiction?
o: Delay in settlement of a claim
Dispute on premium paid or payable
A claim valued at ₹60 lakh including expenses
e: The Ombudsman's pecuniary limit is ₹50 lakh including expenses; claims above it must go to Consumer Commissions or courts. Delay, premium disputes and mis-selling by intermediaries are within jurisdiction.

t: Which of the following is exempt from the compulsory insurance requirement under Section 4 of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991?
o: Central/State Government and Government-owned corporations that establish a fund for relief
e: Section 4(3) exempts the Central Government, State Governments and Government-owned corporations provided they establish and maintain a fund for relief under the Act.

t: A 25-year-old worker (relevant factor 216.91) earning ₹9,000 per month dies in a workplace accident. The employer's liability under the Employees' Compensation Act is:
e: Death compensation = 50% × monthly wages × relevant factor = 50% × 9,000 × 216.91 = ₹9,76,095, which exceeds the minimum of ₹1,20,000.

t: Under Section 3 of the Employees' Compensation Act, the employer is NOT liable for an injury (not resulting in death or permanent total disablement) caused by:
o: Lack of skill of the worker
The worker being under the influence of drink or drugs, or wilful disobedience of safety rules, or wilful removal of safety guards
e: The defences in the proviso to Section 3(1) are drink/drugs, wilful disobedience of express safety orders and wilful removal of safety guards; they do not apply where the injury results in death or permanent total disablement.

t: Section 124 of the Indian Contract Act defines a contract of indemnity as one by which one party promises to:
o: Pay a fixed sum on an event
Save the other from loss caused by the conduct of the promisor himself or any other person
e: Section 124 defines indemnity as a promise to save the other party from loss caused by the promisor or any other person; non-life insurance follows the indemnity principle.

t: An application for relief under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 must be made to the Collector within:
e: Section 6 of the PLI Act requires the application within five years of the occurrence of the accident.

t: Under Section 29A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended), an arbitral award in a domestic arbitration must be made within:
e: Section 29A requires the award within 12 months from the date of completion of pleadings (extendable by 6 months by consent); fast-track arbitration under Section 29B is 6 months.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 norms, a surveyor must be appointed within what time of a claim intimation?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Appointment within 24 hours; survey report within 15 days; insurer's decision within 7 days of the report.

t: IRDAI's October 2023 circular on arbitration clauses in general insurance policies provides that:
o: All policies must contain an arbitration clause
Retail policies shall not contain an arbitration clause; in commercial policies arbitration may be agreed only by mutual consent after a dispute arises
Arbitration is mandatory for claims above ₹50 lakh
e: IRDAI directed removal of arbitration clauses from retail lines of business and made arbitration in commercial policies dependent on mutual consent after the dispute, so policyholders can approach consumer fora.

t: Under Section 12 of the PMLA read with the Rules, records of transactions and identity of clients must be maintained by an insurer for:
o: 5 years from the transaction / end of business relationship
e: Reporting entities must maintain transaction records for five years from the date of transaction and identity records for five years after the business relationship ends.

t: A request under the RTI Act concerning the life or liberty of a person must be answered by the PIO within:
e: Section 7(1) requires information concerning the life or liberty of a person to be provided within 48 hours; ordinary requests get 30 days.
